label: digit 1 input at original position >= 5
explanation: Token detector for the digit 1 when it is input late in the original phase. Fires only in the original phase (none at the delimiter or in the copy phase), and almost exclusively when the input token is 1 (99.8% of activations). It is silent at positions 0-3. At position 4 it fires weakly and only about 40% of the time (0.9% of mass). At positions 5-8 it fires on about every 1 (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude rises with position: mean activation is lower at t=5 and highest at t=7-8, where the top examples reach about 4.2 with 1 as the last original token. It does NOT fire on other digits or letters, or on 1 when 1 is fed back as an input in the copy phase. The leftover recall misses are weak position-4 firings and ~66 tiny activations on other tokens at t=8.

issues: Minor: the step-4 firings (about 41% of '1' inputs at t=4, roughly 17% of active steps) are all tiny, at 0.02-0.06 of the max activation, and carry 0.9% of the mass. I split them by L, by whether the previous token is a digit, and by digit and vowel history. None of these splits separates them: precision stays between 0.38 and 0.57. They look like a soft threshold at onset rather than a missing pattern. Count-based recall (0.828) therefore understates how good the predicate is. Mass recall is 0.991.
Minor: 66 dev activations fall on tokens other than '1'. That is 0.2% of active steps (a few each on v, d, w, m, h), which is scattered noise.

Every factual claim checked out. Activity is zero at the delimiter, in the copy phase, at t 0-3 and at t >= 9. Phase-2 '1' inputs score precision 0 (no firings), and the predicate has 0 false positives on the test split. Mean activation per firing rises with position: about 2.2e-5 mass share per firing at t=5, 3.9e-5 at t=6, 5.0e-5 at t=7 and 5.4e-5 at t=8, which matches 'lowest at t=5, highest at t=7-8'.
